credential.title: One-time setup
credential.why: Homey does not let an app create Flows on its own, so Lightkeeper needs an API key from you. It uses the key only to create and maintain the Flows that connect your remote to your lights.
credential.step1: Open my.homey.app and pick this Homey
credential.step2: Go to Settings → API Keys → New API Key
credential.step3: Tick the Flow permissions, then create it
credential.step4: Copy the key — it is shown only once — and paste it here
credential.malformed: That does not look like a complete API key. Copy the whole key shown when you create it.
credential.expired: The API key is no longer valid. Create a new one in the Homey Web App and enter it here.
credential.noScope: The API key does not have permission to manage Flows. Create a new one with Flow permissions.
credential.unreachable: Could not reach Homey to check the API key. Try again in a moment.

source.title: Choose remote
source.subtitle: Pick the remote, switch or dial you want to use.
source.found: Ready to use — __controls__ buttons and controls detected.
source.unusable: No usable remote events found for this device. Homey does not expose any button or dial events for it, so it cannot be used as a controller.
source.reattach: __name__ looks like the same remote, re-added. Re-attaching keeps every mapping and target exactly as they were.
source.listFailed: No devices were returned. Check the app log for pair/listSources.

targets.title: Choose lights
targets.noLights: No lights were found. Check that your lights are paired and available, then try again.
targets.loadFailed: The lights could not be loaded. Check that Homey is reachable, then try again.

mapping.title: Map controls
mapping.subtitle: Choose which button or gesture performs each lighting function.
mapping.noEvents: This remote exposed no usable events. Go back and pick another.
mapping.unsupportedControl: Lightkeeper cannot build a Flow for __controls__. Map that control to something else, or leave it unassigned.

schedule.title: Set the times
schedule.subtitle: Add one or more schedules. Each turns the lights on at a time you choose, and off again after a while or at another time.
schedule.atMost: At most __max__ schedules on one device. Add a second schedule device for more.
schedule.droppedSome: __count__ schedule(s) are incomplete. Check the times and try again.
schedule.droppedOverlap: __count__ schedule(s) overlap another one on the same lights, so they were not saved. Two windows over the same lights fight — the first to end switches them off.
schedule.timezone: Times follow your Homey's own clock (__zone__).

circadian.title: Follow the day
circadian.subtitle: Set how warm your lights should be through the day. They are set the moment they come on, and follow the curve while they are on.
circadian.alsoBrightnessHelp: Each point also sets how bright the lights are. Only lights that are already on are dimmed — this never switches anything on.
circadian.preStage: Set the colour before the lights come on
circadian.preStageHelp: Lights are then already the right colour the moment they are switched on, with no visible correction. Some lights switch themselves on when their colour is set, so test it here first.
circadian.preStageTesting: Testing on one light that is off…
circadian.preStageOk: __name__ stayed off. Setting the colour in advance is safe on these lights.
circadian.preStageCameOn: __name__ switched itself on, so it has been switched back off and this option turned off. Your lights will be corrected as they come on instead.
circadian.preStageCameOnStuck: __name__ switched itself on and could not be switched back off. This option has been turned off — please switch that light off yourself.
circadian.preStageNoLight: Every light is on right now, so there is nothing to test on. Switch one off and try again.
circadian.atMost: At most __max__ points on one curve.
circadian.needTwo: A curve needs at least __min__ points.
circadian.droppedSome: __count__ point(s) are incomplete. Check the times and try again.
circadian.summary: __count__ point(s) across __lights__ light(s). No Flows are created — this one runs in the app.
circadian.timezone: Times follow your Homey's own clock (__zone__).

state.noConfiguration: This controller has no configuration. Repair it to set it up again.
state.needsCredential: Lightkeeper needs a new API key to manage its Flows.
state.sourceGone: The remote this controller uses is no longer paired.
state.surfaceChanged: This remote now exposes different events. Open repair to remap it.
state.noTargets: None of this controller's lights are available.
state.unsupportedMapping: Lightkeeper could not build a Flow for __controls__. Open Repair and map that control to something else.
state.flowEdited: A Flow this app generated has been edited by hand. Open repair to rebuild it.
state.noSchedule: This schedule has no configuration. Repair it to set it up again.
state.noTimeCard: This Homey does not offer a time trigger Lightkeeper can build on, so the schedule cannot be created. Please report this with your firmware version.
state.noTimezone: Lightkeeper cannot read this Homey's timezone, so it cannot tell which day a schedule belongs to. Restart the app, and report this if it persists.
state.noCurve: This circadian light has no configuration. Repair it to set it up again.
state.noWarmthTargets: None of this device's lights can change colour temperature, so there is nothing for it to do.
state.persistFailed: Lightkeeper could not save what it learned about its Flows. Open repair to try again.

settings.apiKeyExplain: Homey does not let an app create Flows on its own, so Lightkeeper needs an API key from you. Create one at my.homey.app → Settings → API Keys with Flow permissions. Your controllers keep working without it — only the Flows that connect them stop being maintained.
settings.keyValid: A working API key is saved.
settings.keyMissing: No API key saved yet. Lightkeeper cannot create its Flows without one.
settings.keyBroken: The saved API key is not working.
settings.noControllers: No controllers yet. Add one from Devices.
settings.flowsExplain: Lightkeeper creates a Flow for each mapped button, and two for each schedule window. Flows whose Lightkeeper device no longer exists are orphans and can be deleted safely — only Flows this app created and can attribute to a missing device are touched.
settings.orphansFound: __orphans__ orphaned Flow(s) out of __total__ generated, across __live__ live Lightkeeper device(s).
settings.sweepRefused: __total__ generated Flow(s) found, but no Lightkeeper device is running right now. Every Flow would look orphaned, so nothing will be deleted. Check your Lightkeeper devices first.
settings.sweepStale: The list changed while it was on screen, so nothing was deleted. Here it is again.
settings.sweepUnmanaged: __unmanaged__ Flow(s) use a Lightkeeper card but were not created by this app, so they are left alone.
settings.sweeping: Deleting… this can take a while for hundreds of Flows.
settings.pressesExplain: Press a button on your remote, then reload this page. If nothing appears, the generated Flow is not firing. If a row appears but says it was ignored, the reason is shown.
settings.writesExplain: What the app actually sent to each light. An accepted press with no write here means the intent never reached the queue.
settings.requestFailed: The request could not be completed. Try again.
settings.noSchedules: No schedules yet. Add one from Devices.
settings.noCircadian: No circadian lights yet. Add one from Devices.
settings.circadianNow: Now at __warmth__% warmth, next point at __next__
settings.circadianPreStageOff: Setting the colour before the lights come on was turned off automatically: one of these lights switched itself on.
